name: Hesketh Field week
summary: A week camping in a field with sixty other practitioners and a teacher who talks twice a day. The rest of the day is yours, and mostly people talk. Not for beginners. £260.
description:
Every July we put sixty tents in a field under the Long Mynd for a week. There is one teacher, Ros, who has practised in three traditions and settled in none of them, and there are sixty people who have all been practising long enough not to need the basics.

Ros gives a talk at ten and another at five, an hour each, in the marquee. Both are followed by questions, which can run long. Those two hours and their aftermath are the only scheduled thing in the day.

The rest is unscheduled and it is a talking week. Meals are long and loud. People sit in twos and threes in the grass working through what the morning talk did to them. There are unofficial evening discussions that go until midnight. The field is a conversation that lasts seven days, and if what you want is quiet this is emphatically the wrong week; we run a different one for that.

It is a restful week physically. Nobody is asked to sit for long, there is no work, the field is flat, and people sleep a great deal.

We do not teach the fundamentals here and we will not slow down for them. If you have not got a settled practice of some years, the talks will assume things you do not have and the conversations will move too fast. Come to something else first.
practical: Saturday to Saturday, second week of July. £260 including all meals and the field; bring your own tent. Three vegetarian meals a day from the kitchen tent. Compost toilets and solar showers. Church Stretton is the nearest station, four miles; we run a minibus on the Saturdays. Some signal on the hill, none in the field.
